stories.title: Vitalik Buterin Says He's More Confident AI Won't Break Crypto, Backs It With 90% of His Net Worth
stories.summary: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin reportedly said he is now more confident that artificial intelligence will not undermine crypto's core value proposition, and is backing that view by committing roughly 90% of his net worth. CryptoSlate did not provide further detail on how the wager is structured or what prompted his earlier doubts.
stories.whyItMatters: Buterin's public confidence (or lack of it) on AI's effect on crypto's fundamentals carries weight among Ethereum-aligned builders and investors.
whatToWatch: Any follow-up detail on how the 90% commitment is structured
Further comment from Buterin or the Ethereum Foundation on AI-related risk
questions: What does "betting 90% of his net worth" actually involve in practice?
What specific AI threat to crypto was he previously worried about?

sources.title: Vitalik Buterin now confident AI won’t break crypto, betting 90% of his net worth

stories.title: Ethereum's Privacy Push Hits a Gas-Limit Snag as a Simpler Rollup Fix Emerges
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Ethereum's privacy roadmap has run into a technical problem: a single proof reportedly needs nearly twice the gas allowance currently proposed. A separate CryptoSlate report the same day suggested Ethereum may have found a simpler way to ease the computing burden created by its growing rollup ecosystem.
stories.whyItMatters: Gas-cost and proof-design questions directly determine when and how privacy features can actually ship on Ethereum, affecting users and rollups that depend on the roadmap.
whatToWatch: Whether core developers revise the proposed gas allowance
Discussion or adoption of the simpler rollup-load approach
questions: Which specific privacy proof system is running into the gas shortfall?
Would the simpler rollup fix resolve the gas problem or is it unrelated?

sources.title: Ethereum’s privacy push hits a numbers problem: one proof needs nearly twice the proposed gas allowance
Ethereum may have a simpler way to ease the computing burden of its growing rollup ecosystem

stories.title: Harmony Cites AI Threats in Proposal to Shut Down Its Blockchain

stories.whyItMatters: A live blockchain shutting down over AI-linked security concerns would be a notable precedent for how protocols are starting to weigh emerging AI-enabled attack risks.

stories.title: Solana's 'Million-Payments-a-Second' AI Payment System May Leave Sellers Unpaid
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that a Solana-based payment system built to handle a million transactions per second for AI-driven commerce can leave sellers unpaid even after they have delivered goods or services, pointing to a flaw in how the system handles payment finality.
stories.whyItMatters: Settlement flaws in high-throughput payment rails undercut confidence in Solana's push toward AI-agent commerce, a use case it has been promoting heavily.
whatToWatch: Whether the project behind the system issues a fix or a statement
Any confirmed cases of sellers losing funds
questions: Which specific project or protocol built this payment system?
Has any seller actually lost funds because of the flaw so far?

stories.title: Improperly Created Tokens May Explain How $320 Million in Bitcoin Left the Liquid Sidechain

stories.whyItMatters: A $320 million incident on a sidechain used to hold pegged bitcoin is a major event for anyone relying on cross-chain bitcoin infrastructure.

Whether the missing funds are recovered or frozen
Any patch to the token-issuance mechanism involved
questions: Who created the unbacked tokens and how did they bypass the peg controls?
